newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end down on Brazil hedging talk.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end down on Brazil hedging talk.

text.p: CBOT soymeal and soyoil futures ended lower on Wednesday, in line with losses in soybeans, amid talk of active soybean movement in Brazil, traders said.
"Talk of big bean movement in northern Brazil, the biggest yet. There was talk the crushers there were hedging some of their purchases here," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.

Active movement would not bode well for U.S. soy products because it would improve prospects for exports, CBOT sources explained. The market had been supported by reports of a backlog in Brazilian exports and by talk persistent rains in Brazil would delay harvest.
At Brazil's key Paranagua port, three ships were loading soymeal on Wednesday and 14 others were waiting to load soymeal and soybeans, port authorities said.

Soymeal was further pressured by a lack of fund buying interest. The market had been wary of another bout of fund buying like the one that pushed the March and May to contract highs late Tuesday. When the buying interest did not materialize, willing sellers appeared, traders said.
Soymeal ended down $5.10 to $2.70 per ton with March off $5.10 at $256.20. Soyoil closed down 0.42 to 0.10 cent per lb with March off 0.14 at 23.89.
On the day, funds sold at least 1,000 lots soymeal. Dean Witter sold 400 May, Smith Barney sold 200 May and 50 March and Prudential Securities sold 100 March and 200 May.
In soyoil, ADM sold 300 lots May and 300 July, while Cargill Inc bought 400 May and Produce Grain bought 150 March and 50 May, traders said.
In spread trading, SAK Futures spread 500 lots May/March soymeal and Prudential Securities spread 500 July/March.
Tenco Inc spread 500 lots May/March soyoil while Prudential Securities spread 500 March/May. ADM and Cargill Inc each spread 300 March/May.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 30,000 lots, against Tuesday's actual volume of 40,638 lots. Soyoil volume was estimated at 24,000 lots, compared with Tuesday's volume of 31,553 lots.
